correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 43–85. At a leaf all boxes are 1 and diamonds 0; minimum, maximum, and Gödel implication select 0, 1, or one of the finitely many local input values used by the formula. In the summable case apply first Borel–Cantelli to each atom and take the countable intersection first: every formula then has only finitely many strictly positive subthreshold leaf values. Equality with the edge weight contributes 1 to a box, not an exception, and any zero leaf value witnesses the box at once. Summability and positivity of h on positive arguments imply weights tend to zero, so every sequence of diamond candidates tends to zero and its supremum is attained (the zero case uses the root). Conversely for every k the sum of the probabilities of 0<U_n<min(r_n,1/k) diverges, either due to infinitely many r_n≥1/k or by agreement with the original divergent series in the tail. Second Borel–Cantelli on independent leaves and countable intersection give infimum zero for one fixed atom, while all candidates are strictly positive. Countable infima, suprema and witness unions over Borel leaf values give measurable events; root values are irrelevant even at equality. Atoms in μ cause no trouble. The uniform law and the union-bound refinement follow directly. VERIFICATION.md describes analytic checks only; no finite run or formal proof is asserted.

value.rationale: The iff separates two natural questions (every valuation versus almost every valuation) even on the same infinite fuzzy frame. The criterion is directly testable on the law and row weights, handles discrete laws and all formulas at once, and identifies a single atom certifying failure. The star restriction is essential for the selector mechanism, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
